key_insight: Chimera shows that visual diffusion models can scale to much larger contexts by mixing linear-cost state tracking with lightweight attention, instead of relying on full quadratic attention everywhere. This makes it better suited for high-resolution images, long videos, and multimodal inputs.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the prohibitive compute and memory cost of full attention in visual generation models, especially when handling long sequences from images, videos, and text-image-video combinations.
method: Uses a hybrid visual diffusion backbone that processes text, image, and video tokens in one raster-ordered stream without positional embeddings.
Combines Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) for long-context state tracking with O(N) complexity.
Interleaves Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) to keep modeling efficient while preserving expressive visual generation capacity.
Introduces a principled scaling recipe to Chinchilla-scale the model effectively.
impact: For practitioners, Chimera offers a practical path to train and deploy diffusion transformers on much longer and richer visual contexts without the usual quadratic bottleneck. This can improve efficiency for next-generation image generation, video generation, and multimodal creative tools.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing raster-ordered token stream across text, image, and video inputs

Scaling curve chart illustrating improved efficiency at larger model/data sizes
paper_title: Chimera: Designing and Chinchilla-Scaling Hybrid Visual Diffusion Transformers
paper_authors: Chongjian Ge, Hanwen Jiang, Tianyu Wang, Jiuxiang Gu, Yiran Xu
